data.name: Levitiel
data.short_meaning: Connected to Levites in the Hebrew Bible
data.long_meaning: The name Levitiel is derived from the Hebrew word ‘Levi’, which means ‘joined to, attached to, or belonging to God’. Levites were the descendants of the tribe of Levi in ancient Israel, and they were the caretakers of the Tabernacle and the Temple, as well as the teachers and musicians of the congregation. In this sense, the name Levitiel signifies a strong bond with God and a dedication to the sacred duties of the Jewish faith.

in_hebrew.name: לוויטיאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שם כהן-לוי, המקור בעברית, עם פירוש - 'בן-לוי', צאצא לשבט לוי, חלק מקהילת הכהנים, חובתם: לשמש כאבות בית-דין, לשמש כאבות-קהילה, לשמש כאבות-כהנים, ולשמש כאבות-מלכים. כמו כן, כהני-לוי חייכו, שלחו, נהגו, ופלטו, והיו מנהיגי העם.

in_greek.name: Λεβιτιέλ
in_greek.long_meaning: ονομασία καθηκόντων, του Λεβιτιήλ, προέρχεται από την ελληνική, με ετυμολογία - 'υιός-Λευί', θυγατέρα του Λευι, από τη φυλή του Λευι, με ευθύνες: να εξασκούνται ως παππούδες, να εξασκούνται ως παπάδες, να εξασκούνται ως ψάλτες, και να εξασκούνται ως βασιλείς. Αλλά οι Λεβιτιείς, απεικονίζονταν, εξαπέστειλαν, εναργώς, και στάλθηκαν, και ήταν ηγέτες του λαού.

in_latin.name: Levitiel
in_latin.long_meaning: nomen officii, Levitiel, a Latinis, cum origine - 'filius-Levie', filius Levii, de tribu Levi, cum officiis: officiati sunt sacerdotes, officiati sunt pontifices, officiati sunt cantores, et officiati sunt reges. Sed Levitae, imitati sunt, emissi sunt, evidentia sunt, et emissi sunt, et erant principes populi.

in_english.name: Levitiel
in_english.meaning: son of priest, son of Levi
in_english.long_meaning: the name Levitiel, originating from Hebrew roots, with meaning - 'son of Levi', a descendant of the tribe of Levi, a part of the priestly community, with duties: to serve as fathers in the courts, to serve as fathers in the community, to serve as priests, and to serve as kings. Like the Levites, they were portrayed, sent out, evident, and sent out, and were leaders of the people.
